newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine court orders arrests in IBM bribe case.
newsitem.headline: Argentine court orders arrests in IBM bribe case.

text.p: An Argentine court on Tuesday issued arrest warrants for the former head of a national bank and other officials in connection with bribery allegations involving the Argentine unit of U.S. computer maker IBM Corp, local news agencies reported.

Federal Judge Adolfo Bagnasco issued arrest warrants for former Banco Nacion chief Aldo Dadone, former Nacion board member Alfredo Adaco, two former top IBM Argentina executives and a former government official, all of whom have been indicted in the bribery case, the state-run Telam and privately owned DyN news agencies said.
Bagnasco also slapped a $2 million embargo on the private property of each of the men, who include former IBM Argentina president Ricardo Matorana and his deputy Gustavo Soriani .

At least 12 people have been indicted for allegedly covering up bribes that courts believe were paid in 1993 to ensure that IBM's Argentine unit clinched a $250 million deal with the state-run Argentine bank.
IBM Argentina has denied any wrongdoing, but admitted errors and actions "inconsistent with company policy."
